findings.title: No automated test that SQL expressions are disabled
findings.body: The security fix rejects QueryTypeSQL in ReadQuery, but the PR adds no unit test asserting that a SQL expression query fails, including when featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions is enabled. Because this is a regression guard for a critical RCE/LFI issue, a future refactor could accidentally re-enable the SQL path without detection.

findings.title: Feature-flag check in enableSqlExpressions is dead and misleading
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions computes enabled as the negation of FlagSqlExpressions but then returns false in both branches, so the feature toggle has no effect and the conditional is dead. If the intent is a permanent disable, the function should simply return false; otherwise the inverted logic can mislead future changes about how the flag controls SQL expressions.

findings.title: Empty SQL result NoData value is overwritten
findings.body: In SQLCommand.Execute, when frame.Rows() == 0 the code sets rsp.Values to mathexp.NoData but immediately overwrites rsp.Values with mathexp.TableData. As a result the no-data handling branch has no effect, and empty SQL results would be returned as table data if SQL expressions were re-enabled.
